title: This Prehistoric Creature is the Only Ocean-Dwelling Amphibian Ever Discovered - Nautilus
gist: Chinese and American paleontologists describe Gerrothorax maritimus, the first fully marine amphibian, from two nearly complete 240-million-year-old skeletons in China's Guizhou Province. The roughly three-foot, disc-shaped bottom-dweller had bony back armor likely defending against ichthyosaurs.

insights.claim: Paleontologists discovered Gerrothorax maritimus in China's Guizhou Province, the first fully marine amphibian ever found, based on two nearly complete skeletons about 240 million years old.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Pure paleontology finding; no direct market relevance.

insights.claim: Gerrothorax maritimus was about three feet long, disc-shaped and likely an oceanic bottom-dweller with bony back armor that probably defended against ichthyosaurs.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.quote: Its most remarkable feature was bony armor on its back, likely a defense against the many ichthyosaurs swimming in the Triassic oceans.
